paragraphs: Midwives corresponds to O*NET 29-9099.01, providing prenatal care and childbirth assistance. Work covers prenatal assessment, labor monitoring and assistance, emergency response and referral, postpartum follow-up, and records. Conclusions on this page are not clinical diagnoses or prescriptions.

Work context (O*NET work context survey): Characterized by close physical care and frequent communication. 83% report very close physical proximity, 71% have face-to-face discussions daily, and 66% use telephones and email daily.

Abilities and work practices: Maternity medicine and nursing knowledge, assessment and communication skills, and procedural work under pressure. 66% rate the consequences of error as extremely serious, and 44% work more than 40 hours weekly.

Research inputs: The official description, 37 tasks, work activities, work context, and interest code (SR) for O*NET 29-9099.01, plus O*NET-displayed BLS 2025 wages and 2024—2034 employment projections for the parent category Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Workers, All Other.
Inputs: Pregnant and postpartum patients and newborns, maternity health information, examination and monitoring equipment, and care and follow-up records.
Inspectable outputs: Prenatal assessments and care plans, childbirth and emergency response records, postpartum follow-up and health education materials, and referral and certification documents.
Occupational boundary: This page covers only O*NET 29-9099.01 Midwives. Tools or proxy statistics cannot substitute for adjacent nursing and medical occupations or prescribing and sign-off authority.

Adjacent relationships are for comparing directions only: This occupation centers on maternity care and childbirth assistance. Registered nurses provide general clinical nursing, nurse practitioners and physician assistants cover broader diagnosis and treatment, and obstetricians / gynecologists and family physicians bear higher-risk treatment and surgical responsibilities.
Compare each point: Who provides maternity care, who has prescribing and sign-off authority, and who handles surgery and emergencies? Similar titles do not mean identical duties or authority.
Difference from registered nurses: They provide broad clinical nursing; this occupation focuses on maternity care and childbirth assistance.
Difference from nurse practitioners: They address broader conditions and populations; this occupation centers on maternity care.
Difference from obstetricians and gynecologists: They bear higher-risk treatment and surgical responsibilities. This occupation's scope and authorization are defined by local rules.

risks.mitigation: Assess under standards and track changes; qualified people confirm care plans.
risks.scenario: Prenatal assessment or risk judgment bias may miss referral needs.
risks.title: Prenatal assessment bias

risks.consequence: May delay necessary treatment and affect maternal and infant safety.
risks.mitigation: Refer promptly under risk checklists and escalation criteria and retain records.
risks.scenario: Delayed referral: Failing to escalate promptly when signs such as gestational hypertension or preterm labor appear.
risks.title: Referral delays

risks.consequence: May endanger maternal and infant life and health.
risks.mitigation: Follow institutional emergency plans and retain response records.
risks.scenario: Nonstandard emergency responses: Failure to follow plans for difficult labor, postpartum hemorrhage, or newborn resuscitation.
risks.title: Emergency response deviations

risks.affected_roles: Midwives and relevant personnel accessing patient records.
risks.consequence: May violate privacy and compliance requirements and damage trust.
risks.mitigation: Handle data under privacy and minimum-necessary principles and limit access.
risks.scenario: Patient information leakage: Improper access to or sharing of maternity and health information.
risks.title: Patient information protection

risks.affected_roles: Midwives responsible for records and certificates.
risks.consequence: Affects traceability and continuity of care.
risks.mitigation: Keep complete audit trails under recording standards and review.
risks.scenario: Incomplete or incorrect records: Missing visit, intervention, and follow-up records.
risks.title: Records and continuity of care

risks.affected_roles: Midwives and institutional clinical responsibility chains.
risks.consequence: Can prevent increased risk from insufficient evidence or exceeded authority.
risks.mitigation: Retain records and escalate through institutional procedures.
risks.scenario: Shared escalation rule: For uncertain assessments, emergencies, or privacy questions, first stabilize care under plans and limit information dissemination. Refer facts and unresolved questions to authorized people for confirmation.
risks.title: Clinical escalation and handover
